_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
The test shrinks the app's tail-first mounting so that a 15-turn conversation at /c/{{SLUG}} spans many chunks: on load only the last few chunks mount (as ".messages-chunk" elements) and older history renders as placeholders ([data-testid="pending-chunk"]). "The counts" are pending = document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="pending-chunk"]').length and mounted = document.querySelectorAll('.messages-chunk').length. "The gap" is the messages container's (".messages-container") scrollHeight - scrollTop - clientHeight. To "open the conversation", navigate to /c/{{SLUG}}, wait for the message input ([data-testid="message-input"]) to be visible (allow 30s), then wait until the LAST element matching [data-testid="message"] is visible (its getBoundingClientRect() has a non-zero width and height; allow 30s). The test has already set the shelley.tailFirstTest knob; do not set it yourself. Check every assertion with an eval that has "expect" (or an assert_* or wait_* step): an eval without "expect" asserts nothing. Wait with such steps and a timeout, not with polling loops inside the expression. When a step says to record something, do it in one eval without "expect" that stores it in the named window variable, then check that variable in a separate eval with "expect". Perform the steps in order. A cached refresh keeps history unmounted while waiting for the server; the background sweep is off and the conversation, {{ID}}, is archived. Once call "hold" has run, the server's answers to incremental loads of the conversation (a GET of /api/conversation/{{ID}} with a last_sequence_id query parameter) are held back until call "release"; call "incremental" says whether such a load has arrived ("true" or "false").
1. Navigate to /c/{{SLUG}}.
2. Wait until window.__shelleyPerf?.loads().some((load) => load.conversationId === "{{ID}}") is true.
3. Record the counts: window.__initial = {pending, mounted}. window.__initial.pending must be greater than 0.
4. Leave the conversation the way the router would: eval history.pushState({}, "", "/new") and then dispatch a PopStateEvent("popstate") on window.
5. Wait until there are exactly 0 [data-testid="message"] elements.
6. Call "hold".
7. Go back in the browser history, as its back button does (the app pushed that entry, so the same document stays loaded and window.__initial survives).
8. Call "incremental" until it returns "true".
9. Wait until the last [data-testid="message"] element is visible (non-zero width and height).
10. While the incremental load is still held, record the counts in window.__refreshing = {pending, mounted}; then JSON.stringify({pending: window.__refreshing.pending > 0, fewer: window.__refreshing.mounted < window.__initial.pending + window.__initial.mounted, overlays: document.querySelectorAll(".conversation-loading-overlay").length}) must be exactly {"pending":true,"fewer":true,"overlays":0}.
11. Call "release".
12. Wait until window.__shelleyPerf.loads().filter((load) => load.conversationId === "{{ID}}").length is exactly 2.
13. pending must still be greater than 0.

steps.expression: (function(){ var els = document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="message"]'); if (!els.length) return false; var last = els[els.length-1]; var r = last.getBoundingClientRect(); return r.width > 0 && r.height > 0; })()

JSON.stringify({pending: window.__refreshing.pending > 0, fewer: window.__refreshing.mounted < window.__initial.pending + window.__initial.mounted, overlays: document.querySelectorAll('.conversation-loading-overlay').length})
